chapter_theme: The greatness of the Lord's devotees: where one lives the land prospers and rain falls, they attain the Lord in this body and this world, all things are held in their sight, and they are bound to Siva by a deed written before birth.
structure_note: The chapter opens and nearly closes on the land blessed by a devotee's presence (1868, 1869, 1881, 1882). Between them come verses in the devotee's own voice, on holding all in the hand and the eye (1870, 1871), on the Lord beyond sex and sense (1872), on the inner chamber (1874, 1877) and on the deed of servitude (1876). 1883 ends with the devotees at the top of a ladder of knowers.

1868.reading: If there is one who seeks the god of all directions in the fitting way, there are no enemies, rain falls on the earth, and that world suffers no inner want or ruin.
1868.nuance: ஒரு வாது இருக்கில் is odd; it is probably ஒருவன் இருக்கில், 'if there is one'. On the plain sense a single seeker of the Lord brings peace and rain to his whole land.

1869.reading: Born in that world, with that very body they seek rare austerity in that world, join Hara's feet in that world and gain grace in that world.
1869.nuance: அவ்வுலகம் may be the land of 1868 where the devotee lives, or this world as against another. Either way the stress falls on attaining in the same body and the same world one is born in, not after death.

1870.reading: If the sign I have taken, the summit of the great mountain, the gods, the immortals of the cosmos, the Primal one and those of the eight directions all come into the palm of my hand, then we are saved for good.
1870.nuance: கொண்ட குறி (the sign taken) may be the linga or the form of the Lord meditated on, and குலவரை உச்சி Kailasa. The verse may be a condition or a claim: the devotee who holds the Lord holds everything.

1871.reading: The seven worlds, the undivided, the soul, all the moving and unmoving, the qualities, the ancient Veda, creation, protection and the rest, and Siva who beholds them: none is apart from my eye.
1871.nuance: என் கண் can be the eye of knowledge that sees all, or the devotee's eye in which all is contained. கண்ட சிவன் may also mean 'the Siva I have seen'.

1872.reading: The light within the dark, neither woman nor man nor neuter, cannot be known by anyone; he sees without eyes and hears without ears, and to have searched out the Lord's greatness is true maturity.
1872.nuance: மூடத்துள் may be the body, ignorance, or the hidden heart. மூப்பு (age, seniority) is taken as ripeness of wisdom; the line could also mean that inquiring into his greatness only ends in old age.

1873.reading: In this moving world the Lord's devotees go by the undeluded way and rule the world of the sky; their arms are the eight directions, their feet the netherworld, and their great crown the outer cosmos.
1873.nuance: The second half gives the devotee the cosmic body usually given to the Lord. போது பாதாளம் is read as 'the feet reach the netherworld'; பகிரண்டம் is the outer cosmos.

1874.reading: Contemplate our Lord who dwells in the inner chamber; those who have seen the inner chamber will not come to grief; the heart that enters within and knows, seeing the inner chamber, can destroy the eight.
1874.nuance: அகம்படி is the inner apartment of a palace and those who serve in it, and also simply 'within'; the verse uses it in every line. The eight (எட்டு) to be destroyed are not named; the eight bodily constituents or eight bonds are possible.

1875.reading: The first Lord, who stood as end and beginning, as love's companion and as destruction, has taken my soul as his field to plough; blame and praise and all that befalls me now fall away.
1875.nuance: உழவு கொண்டான் pictures the Lord tilling the soul. Taking கழிவும் முதலும் as end and beginning is the usual reading; காதல் துணை may also be his consort.

1876.reading: For my mother, my father and seven times seven births, a deed of bond to Siva was written that very day; he who alone created the world wrote it, and the cloud-coloured one stood as witness.
1876.nuance: ஆவணம் is a legal deed, here a deed of servitude, and நேர்எழுத்து the attesting signature, so Brahma writes it and Vishnu witnesses it. The image of hereditary bondage to Siva by deed resembles the story told of Sundarar. Sengalvaraya cites Appar's 'முந்தி உலகம் படைத்தான்'.

1877.reading: He dwells close within the resolute, flows like milk within the humble, and stands as the Primal Lord within those who wear his signs; for one who has reckoned him so, can he be let go?
1877.nuance: The last line is unclear: it may ask whether such a devotee could ever be abandoned, or whether he could ever give the Lord up. அணிந்தார் may be those who wear ash and rudraksha, or those who adorn the Lord.

1878.reading: Nandi of the hanging locks, above the heads of the gods, placed his devotees on his head as a garland so that they might do true service; the one of spreading locks rules the golden world free of baseness and grants its fruit.
1878.nuance: மிலை is a garland worn on the head; who is placed there is not said, and some take it as the Lord placing his feet on the devotee's head. The golden world (பொன்னுலகு) recurs from 1867.

1879.reading: To recognise Hara's devotees by their signs and delight in them even at an age that does not yet understand is true servitude; those who walk with the matted crown of his sign, bathing in wave-filled waters, make great austerity.
1879.nuance: அறியாப் பருவம் is childhood, the time before understanding; the verse may be thinking of child saints like Sambandar. மறியார் புனல் may also be the waters of the Ganga in the locks of the one who holds the deer (மறி).

1880.reading: Those who approach him and love him are able to approach Siva too; for the devotees who draw near and seek him, greatness in him becomes absorption.
1880.nuance: அவன் is most likely the devotee or the guru, so that approaching him is approaching Siva; இலயம் is absorption. The referents of அவன் and இவன் are not fixed by the verse.

1881.reading: The eight classes of gods who were there before come in countless numbers with love to this wide earth, and across the directions and the sky alike the land for twelve leagues around is made fit.
1881.nuance: The verse continues the theme of the place where a devotee lives. எண்இரு நாலு திசை and பன்னிரு காதம் are numbers whose exact sense is unclear; பதஞ்செய்யும் may mean 'becomes ripe' or 'becomes a holy station'.

1882.reading: The land where a Siva-yogi and jnani dwell will have knowers free of false yoga; the ninefold yoga will be gained, good order will be seen, and without the yoga of births it becomes the higher world.
1882.nuance: அவயோகம் (bad yoga), நவயோகம் (nine yogas or new yoga) and பவயோகம் (union with birth) form a play on யோகம். The nine yogas are not specified.

1883.reading: He who created the vast world knows from above; he who transcends the vast world knows from above; the immortals of the vast world know from above; and Siva's true devotees know from above.
1883.nuance: The four lines repeat மேலுணர், so the devotees end a ladder beginning with the Creator and Siva. மேலுணர்வான் may also mean 'the one known as highest', which would make the verse a list of who is supreme.

links.note: Both say the land where a devotee lives is blessed: 1868 with peace and rain, 1882 with true knowers and good order, and release from births.
The Kural makes giving and austerity depend on rain; Tirumular runs it the other way, making rain depend on the presence of one who seeks the Lord.
Both speak of Tirumular as bound and sent by the Lord: 1863 as Nandi's message, 1876 by a deed of servitude written before birth.

1868 says that where one person seeks the Lord in the fitting way, 'பார்மழை பெய்யும்', rain falls and the land lacks nothing. Kural 55 says the wife who worships her husband commands the rain: 'பெய்யெனப் பெய்யும் மழை'. Both make one person's devotion, to the Lord in one case and to the husband in the other, the cause of rain for everyone.

1869 insists the devotee attains Hara's feet and grace 'அவ்வுடலோடும்', in the very body he was born with, in this same world. 724 gives the reason that body must be kept: 'உடம்பார் அழியில் உயிரார் அழிவர்', without the body true knowledge cannot be won, so 'உடம்பை வளர்த்தேன் உயிர்வளர்த்தேனே'. 724 supplies the method behind 1869's claim.

1871 says the seven worlds, all beings, the Veda, the five acts and Siva himself are not apart from 'என் கண்', the knower's eye. 1909 says of the Siva-jnani that Siva is 'எங்கும்' for him and that, dying here, he stands everywhere. 1871 puts everything within the knower's sight; 1909 carries the knower out into everything.

1872 says the light within is 'பெண்ணல்ல ஆணல்ல பேடல்ல', neither woman, man nor neuter, and cannot be known. 434 praises the First 'ஆண்பெண் அலியுரு வாய்நின்ற', standing in the form of male, female and neuter. On a literal reading one denies him all three forms and the other gives him all three; the conflict eases if 434 means immanence and 1872 transcendence.

3004 gives the Lord a cosmic body: the world-eggs are his crown and his red feet reach 'பாதாளம்', the underworld. 1873 gives this same body to the devotees: their arms are the eight directions, their feet the 'பாதாள', their crown the 'பகிரண்டம்'. The pairing shows the chapter on the devotee's greatness transferring the Lord's own cosmic image to his servants.

1874 tells us to contemplate the Lord who dwells in 'அகம்படி', the inner chamber, and says those who enter it escape grief. 2605 places Nandi 'மெய்த்தாள் அகம்படி', in the inner apartment behind a bolt no hand can open until falsehood is put away. Both use the palace's inner quarters for the Lord's place in the heart; 2605 adds what bars the way in.

1875 says the first Lord 'என் ஆவி உழவுகொண்டானே', has taken my soul to plough, so praise and blame fall away. 1886 says the field is fenced and 'உச்சிக்கு முன்னே உழவு சமைந்தது', the ploughing is done before noon, yet the fearful will not reap and eat and go begging instead. Read together, the Lord does the ploughing and the soul is left only to harvest.

1876 says a deed of bondage (ஆவணம்) to Siva was written for my mother, father and seven times seven births, with Brahma writing and Vishnu witnessing. Thiruppugazh 403 retells Siva coming as an old man to a youth's wedding, claiming him 'இவன் அடிமை' and producing 'பழைய ... ஆவணத்தை', the old deed the youth tore. Both rest on the image of hereditary servitude to Siva fixed by a written deed.

1879 calls it true servitude to recognise Hara's devotees 'குறியால்', by their signs, and delight in them. 1660 warns that 'பொய்வேடம் மெய்வேடம் போலவே பூணினும்', the false garb is worn just like the true, and the garb saves only those who know. 1660 limits 1879: the outward sign does not by itself mark a true devotee.

1880 says those who approach 'அவன்', the devotee, with love can approach Siva too. 2624 says the poet became servant of the servants of his servants, and 'அடியார் அருளால் அவனடி கூட', it was by the devotees' grace that he reached the Lord's feet. Both route the way to Siva through his devotees.

1880 says approaching the devotee with love is the way to approach Siva. Thiruppugazh 484, sunk in the sea of desire, asks for one remedy: 'உனது அடியாராகிய மோன ஞானிகளுடனே சேரவும் அருள்வாயே', grace to join the Lord's silent devotees. The song turns 1880's teaching into a prayer.

source_issues: 1869: line 1 reads உடலோணடும், a misprint for உடலோடும்.
1883: line 4 reads மேலுணுர், a misprint for மேலுணர்.
1868: ஒரு வாது இருக்கில் is probably a misdivision of ஒருவன் இருக்கில்.
